selfcare:anxietyBreathwork.description: Four equal phases — inhale, hold, exhale, hold — used by everyone from athletes to Navy SEALs to steady focus under pressure.
selfcare:anxietyBreathwork.name: Box Breathing

selfcare:anxietyBreathwork.description: Dr. Andrew Weil's technique — a longer exhale than inhale shifts the body toward rest. Good before sleep or when winding down from a spike.
selfcare:anxietyBreathwork.name: 4-7-8 Breathing

selfcare:anxietyBreathwork.description: A gentle, even 5-second in / 5-second out rhythm (about 6 breaths a minute) — a steady baseline for everyday calm, no holds to track.
selfcare:anxietyBreathwork.name: Coherent Breathing

selfcare:anxietyBreathwork.description: A short inhale and a long, slow exhale — the fastest way to nudge the nervous system down when anxiety spikes in the moment.
selfcare:anxietyBreathwork.name: Extended Exhale

selfcare:anxietyTips.body: Name 5 things you can see, 4 you can touch, 3 you can hear, 2 you can smell, and 1 you can taste. Pulls attention out of a spiraling thought and back into the room.
selfcare:anxietyTips.title: 5-4-3-2-1 Grounding

selfcare:anxietyTips.body: A quick burst of cold (splash your face, hold an ice cube, run cold water over your wrists) triggers the dive reflex and can blunt a panic spike within seconds.
selfcare:anxietyTips.title: Cold water on your wrists or face

selfcare:anxietyTips.body: Instead of "this is stupid, stop thinking it," try "I’m noticing an anxious thought about X." Labeling creates a little distance without fighting it.
selfcare:anxietyTips.title: Name the thought, don’t argue with it

selfcare:anxietyTips.body: You don't need a whole conversation. A single low-stakes message to someone you trust breaks the isolation a spiral thrives on.
selfcare:anxietyTips.title: Text one person

selfcare:anxietyTips.body: Tense each muscle group for 5 seconds, then release, working head to toe. The contrast makes it easier to actually feel your body relax.
selfcare:anxietyTips.title: Progressive muscle relaxation

selfcare:anxietyTips.body: Anxious thoughts are often harsher than anything you’d say to someone else in the same spot. Borrowing that kinder voice is a real reframing tool, not just a platitude.
selfcare:anxietyTips.title: Ask "what would I tell a friend?"

selfcare:anxietyTips.body: A small, physical anchor. Notice the actual pressure of the floor under your feet for a few breaths — it’s hard to fully spiral while paying attention to something this concrete.
selfcare:anxietyTips.title: Put both feet flat on the floor
